title: Room typed on a loose drawing slides it instead of growing around it
goal: Type room into the Layout section of a group that arranges nothing and the whole drawing slides across and down by that much instead of the box growing outward around it. Nothing on screen gets roomier, it just moves. Room on a group like that should leave everything exactly where it was put and grow the box outward, which is what that arrangement promises everywhere else.
notes: GroupFlow.closedAround moves the contents to padding.left/padding.top and Layer.arrangedBounds keeps the frame origin, so the contents move and the box grows down and right. Growing outward means also moving the layer frame by -dx/-dy in GroupFlow.flowing; it is idempotent, because the second pass computes dx = 0. Careful with the case a surface is present: there the top left is anchored today and a button grows to the right, which is right and must not change. Found while fixing more-room-on-a-copy-moves-it-instead-of-making-i on 2026-09-07: the copy knob was taken off drawings like this, but the inspector still offers it.
acceptance: Typing room into the Layout section of a group set to Free leaves every piece inside it exactly where it was on the canvas
The group box grows outward by that much on every side that is the size of its contents
A group with a surface in it still grows the way it does today, so a button does not start moving when its room changes

log.note: Adversarial review before building: the mock is not involved here, this is a plain broken promise. Free means things stay where you put them, and room was the one field that broke that promise. Shortest version that delivers the value: move the group's own frame back by exactly what the contents moved in, which is idempotent because the second pass computes zero. No new UI, no new field, no decision needed.

Reproduced first, before touching anything: a Free group at (100,50) holding two boxes, given 16 of room, came out as box (100,50,132,92) with contents at local (16,16) and (76,56), so on the canvas the drawing had slid from (100,50) to (116,66) and the box had grown only right and down.

Fix: GroupFlow.placed now returns Settled (children plus a grew vector) and GroupFlow.flowing offsets the group's own frame by -grew. The vector is only non-zero on an axis with no size of its own, and only where nothing in the group is a surface, so a button still grows right and down from the corner it is pinned at. Empty groups return zero so nothing can drift.

TDD: five new tests in GroupHugTests and one document-level test in GroupPaddingTests (typing room through History, plus undo). Confirmed they all fail with the fix removed and pass with it. Updated the one existing test that encoded the old box origin. Whole suite: 4790 tests, 403 suites, green.

Verified live on the probe app (Screen Recording granted, real window captures). A rectangle and an ellipse grouped: before, X 200 Y 160 W 280 H 200, Padding 0; after typing 40, X 160 Y 120 W 360 H 280, Padding 40, and the document renders before, after and post-undo are byte for byte identical, so nothing on the canvas moved. Starter Button given 32 of room: X 261 Y 232 unchanged, W 78 -> 110, so the surface case is untouched.
Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-08-room-grows-outward.json with two real screenshots. Design doc updated (docs/design/ui-building.md, 'A hugging axis takes that axis over').

Left alone on purpose: Layer.spendsRoom still hides the room knob on a component copy of a fill-less drawing. The room is correct now but still invisible on a group that paints nothing, so that gate is still the right call; raised as a question in the audit instead of changed here.
